title: Compact sources factor through a stage of a closed T1 chain
statement: Let $\lambda$ be a nonzero limit ordinal and $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha<\lambda}$ a continuous ordinal chain of topological spaces: at every nonzero limit $\beta<\lambda$, $X_\beta$ has the colimit topology. Suppose each successor map is a closed $T_1$ inclusion, meaning an injective continuous map which identifies its source with a closed subspace of its target and for which each point outside the image is closed in the target. Give $X=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\lambda}X_\alpha$ the final topology on the set-theoretic union. Let $A$ be a compact topological space (every open cover has a finite subcover). Every continuous map $A\to X$ factors continuously through some $X_\alpha$. Equivalently, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\lambda}\operatorname{Cont}(A,X_\alpha)\to\operatorname{Cont}(A,X)$ is bijective. Colimits are understood by the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2, printed pp. 49-50: compact topological spaces are finite relative to closed T1 inclusions. Read the PDF online and in the sandbox; no Stacks tag states this topological assertion.

proof.text: Identify stages with their images in the set-theoretic union and put $X_\lambda=X$. Fix $\alpha<\lambda$ and a closed subset $F\subseteq X_\alpha$. Induct on $\beta\geq\alpha$: $F$ is closed in $X_\alpha$; a successor closed embedding carries it to a closed set; at a limit $\beta$, its inverse images in stages $\gamma\geq\alpha$ are closed by induction and in stages $\gamma<\alpha$ are closed by continuity into $X_\alpha$, so the final topology makes $F$ closed in $X_\beta$. This includes $\beta=\lambda$. In particular $X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_\beta$ is a closed embedding: it is continuous and injective, and every closed subset of its source remains closed in its target, which gives precisely the subspace topology.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.1 and Proposition 2.4.2, printed p. 49: explicit closed-subset induction establishing embeddings into each later stage.

proof.text: Every point $x\in X\setminus X_0$ has a least stage $\delta$ of occurrence. This stage is a successor $\eta+1$: it is not zero, and at a nonzero limit the underlying colimit is the union of the earlier stages. The successor closed $T_1$ condition makes $\{x\}$ closed in $X_{\eta+1}$; step 1 makes it closed in every later stage including $X$. Thus each selected point outside $X_0$ below has a closed singleton, even though points of $X_0$ need not be closed.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2, printed pp. 49-50: relative T1 property, expanded using the least stage of occurrence.

proof.text: Let $f:A\to X$ be continuous and suppose its image is contained in no stage. Starting with $\alpha_0=0$, choose $x_n\in f(A)\setminus X_{\alpha_{n-1}}$ and a stage $\alpha_n$ containing it, for $n\geq1$. Necessarily $\alpha_n>\alpha_{n-1}$, and the points are distinct. Put $\mu=\sup_{n\geq0}\alpha_n\leq\lambda$ and $S=\{x_n:n\geq1\}$. The strict increase shows that $\mu$ is a nonzero limit, all $\alpha_n<\mu$, and the stages $\alpha_n$ are cofinal below $\mu$. Use $X_\mu$ when $\mu<\lambda$ and $X_\lambda=X$ when $\mu=\lambda$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2, printed p. 50: sequence of points and its supremum ordinal.

proof.text: Fix $T\subseteq S$ and $\beta<\mu$. Choose $n$ with $\beta\leq\alpha_n$. For $m>n$, $x_m\notin X_{\alpha_{m-1}}\supseteq X_\beta$, so $T\cap X_\beta\subseteq\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$. This intersection is a finite union of closed singletons by step 2, hence closed. The final topology at $\mu$ makes $T$ closed in $X_\mu$; step 1 makes it closed in $X$ when $\mu<\lambda$. Therefore every subset $T$ of $S$, including $S$ and $S\setminus\{x_n\}$, is closed in $X$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2, printed p. 50: every subset of the sequence is closed in the supremum stage; closedness in the full union made explicit.

proof.text: The opens $V_0=X\setminus S$ and $V_n=X\setminus(S\setminus\{x_n\})$ for $n\geq1$ cover $X$: $V_0$ covers its complement of $S$, and $x_n\in V_n$. Their inverse images under $f$ form an open cover of $A$. Compactness supplies a finite subcover. But $V_0$ meets none of $S$, and each $V_n$ meets $S$ only in $x_n$, so this finite family misses some $x_m\in S\subseteq f(A)$. Any preimage of that point is uncovered, a contradiction. Hence $f(A)\subseteq X_\alpha$ for some $\alpha<\lambda$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2, printed p. 50: compactness contradiction, written directly as an open cover of the original compact source.

proof.text: Choose $\alpha$ from step 5 and define $g:A\to X_\alpha$ as the unique set map lifting $f$. For an open $U\subseteq X_\alpha$, step 1 gives an open $V\subseteq X$ with $U=V\cap X_\alpha$; thus $g^{-1}(U)=f^{-1}(V)$ is open. Hence $g$ is continuous and the factorization holds, including $A=\varnothing$ (which already factors through $X_0$).

source.place: Lemma 2.4.1 and Proposition 2.4.2, printed p. 49: a set factorization through an embedded stage is continuous.

proof.text: The compatible postcomposition maps define the canonical map of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Explicitly the set colimit is the disjoint union of $\operatorname{Cont}(A,X_\alpha)$ modulo identifying a map with its postcomposition to a later stage: compatible families descend uniquely through this quotient, verifying the stated universal property. Step 6 proves surjectivity. If maps at stages $\alpha$ and $\beta$ induce the same map to $X$, take $\gamma=\max(\alpha,\beta)<\lambda$. Their postcomposites into $X_\gamma$ agree pointwise since $X_\gamma\to X$ is injective, so they represent the same quotient element. This proves injectivity and the equivalent bijection.

source.place: Section 2.4, printed p. 49 (colimits of sets with final topology), and Proposition 2.4.2: explicit quotient and bijection argument.

lean.statement: theorem compact_closedT1_chain_factorization (κ : Ordinal.{u}) (hκ : Order.IsSuccLimit κ) (F : Set.Iio κ ⥤ TopCat.{v}) [F.IsWellOrderContinuous] (hclosed : ∀ (i j : Set.Iio κ) (hij : i ⋖ j), IsClosedEmbedding (F.map (homOfLE hij.le))) (hT1 : ∀ (i j : Set.Iio κ) (hij : i ⋖ j) (y : F.obj j), y ∉ Set.range (F.map (homOfLE hij.le)) → IsClosed ({y} : Set (F.obj j))) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (A : TopCat.{v}) [CompactSpace A] : (∀ f : A ⟶ c.pt, ∃ (i : Set.Iio κ) (g : A ⟶ F.obj i), g ≫ c.ι.app i = f) ∧ ∀ (s : Cocone (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op A))) (hs : IsColimit s), Function.Bijective (hs.desc ((coyoneda.obj (op A)).mapCocone c))
lean.note: The final-topology union is represented by an arbitrary TopCat colimit cocone. The second conjunct asserts bijectivity of the canonical IsColimit.desc for every chosen colimit cocone of the continuous-map-set diagram; no extra existence assumption is placed on the factorization conclusion.
